source_caption:
The scene where Jordan hits on Naomi’s aunt in The Wolf of Wall Street is funny because Leonardo DiCaprio plays it with total shameless confidence, as if Jordan’s ego has completely erased any sense of normal social behavior. It’s a perfect snapshot of the character’s world: no boundary is too obvious, no situation is too inappropriate, and every room becomes another performance.

The Wolf of Wall Street (2013), directed by Martin Scorsese, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Jonah Hill, Margot Robbie. A wild and electrifying rise-and-fall saga about greed, excess, and corruption, capturing Wall Street ambition with outrageous energy and unforgettable performances.

source_details.title: The Wolf of Wall Street
source_details.synopsis: The Wolf of Wall Street is a 2013 American biographical film co-produced and directed by Martin Scorsese, written by Terence Winter, and based on Jordan Belfort's 2007 memoir. It loosely recounts Belfort's career as a stockbroker in New York City and how his firm, Stratton Oakmont, engaged in rampant corruption and fraud on Wall Street, leading to his downfall. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Belfort; Jonah Hill as his business partner and friend Donnie Azoff; Margot Robbie as his second wife, Naomi Lapaglia; Matthew McConaughey as his mentor and former boss Mark Hanna; and Kyle Chandler as FBI special agent Patrick Denham portraying Gregory Coleman. It is DiCaprio's fifth collaboration
